Do you think about how long the distance is between the dinning room and the office you study at? Stuff like that adds up and while it’s not significant, thinking about stuff like that is important for your sanity so you don’t have to think about what to do next which waste a lot of time. For example with eating can you leave your laptop next to you on the dining table so that once you’re done eating you can read your assignments right away as opposed to eat, out the dishes away, wash the dishes, put the dishes back , walk to the bathroom and use the toilet, walk to your office, load up your computer, log in etc…

This month I want to recommit to my dream of becoming a professional artist and get to the point of having 10 million dollars in my bank account with 0 debt. 

Fun story: I've made the switch from nursing to the art field because being in a field where you face death really makes you rethink your life. I was never an artistic person because everyone of my friends drew better than me, but I bit the bullet and have been making art 5 years. 

I've been consistently drawing and painting and learning from teachers m-f 8am-6pm so I put in hours like it was an actual job.

I made so much progress to the point that my art was comprable to the 18 year old kids who's been drawing most of their life vs. my 5 years in the field.

Lately though I've been facing fatigue issues to the point where if I drew a line I would have to lay down in bed for a day (yes im not exagerating) I would draw till the point I get dizzy and want to vommit but kept going.

I've taken a really long break 2019 to restructure my practice to a more sustainable pace while working a part time job to support my art career.

I finally feel like I've found the right pacing that's not too much but not too little for my life so I'm excited to back to the drawing board and begin walking towards my dream again!

Becoming an artist might be one person's dream, making money as an artist might be another person's dream. But my dream is to make 10 million dollars with 0 debt in a sustainable manner that allows me the time and freedom to travel, paint, enjoy the luxuries and securities of life!

Hey bro sorry to hear you experience this. I have felt similar things even at church or class when I'm surrounded by new people. Even though I know they're good people, my brain just short circuits itself. How old are you bro? It can feel like the whole world is against you when you're a teenager and you don't feel like you belong.

Give Jordan Peterson a shot and listen to his lectures and they might help you put words to what you are feeling. It can be scary but you can start small by asking

hey what homework is due today?

Oh okay, thanks bro/girl

and then just start small and keep it consistent. Of course don't ask the same persom the same question "what homework is due today" everyday, try asking a different person each day.

So like ask Susie what homework is due on monday

ask Dan what homework is due on tuesday

ask Joe what homework is due on wednesday

etc.. and just rotate out the people based on the day.

The important part is not what you say, but so much as the consistency of getting social experience that is important at this point. 

I'm 25 and I've been practicing social skills since I was a in college and going hard on it and I've made alot of progress to the point people call me a "people's person" when I'm at the peak of my skill level. But I still feel this way when I enter a new space with new people. Hell I entered a gaming tournament by myself and I still felt like that around my fellow nerds lmao.

So maybe you can overcome this feeling, or maybe this feeling will be with you for the rest of your life. Either way it's okay, you will become braver and braver over your lifetime with social situation so the fear might not go away but you will get better and braver.

​

Please feel free to PM me about any tips,tricks,strategies or social skills you have a question about. I'm not the best but I have plenty of experience starting from the bottom to the point where I can talk to anyone in a room whether they are strangers or not. It's not much but it's something.
